prompt.context: Your client has a chain of hotels across the USA with locations primarily in gambling cities (e.g. Las Vegas and Atlantic City). The client has been in the business for a number of years and is particularly concerned with the performance of their hotel in Las Vegas. They have come to your firm for advice on how to improve the overall business, but specifically the performance of the Las Vegas Hotel. The Las Vegas hotel is old and requires modernization.
prompt.question: Should the client knock down the hotel and start again, or renovate whilst open for business? What factors would you consider in helping the client, and what recommendations would you give?

clarifying_info.q: Does each hotel have a casino?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, each hotel has a casino.
All hotels are profitable; assume equally profitable.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's financial position?
clarifying_info.a: Family-owned business. Shareholders are risk averse. Sufficient funds are available; any future investment can be funded through equity. Lack of liquidity in the market is not a concern.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's competitive position?
clarifying_info.a: Second tier of hotels behind the major hotels, e.g. the Mirage.
No calculations are required. At most, discuss how calculations would be made.

framework: Define the two options: (1) knock down and rebuild, (2) renovate while open
Assess financial impact: revenue foregone vs. incremental profitability from modernization
Evaluate operational factors: construction timeline, staff management, brand presence
Identify risks for each option: execution risk, brand risk, competitive response
Consider other issues: specific renovations needed, lessons from competitors, post-completion launch
Synthesize into a recommendation backed by the client's risk profile and strategic goals

questions.prompt: What are the key trade-offs for Option 1 (knock down and rebuild)?
questions.guidance: Candidate should cover: loss of revenue during full closure vs. higher incremental profitability once rebuilt; shorter construction period and greater scope to redesign layout and brand; cash outflow items (construction costs, rebranding); staff management (fire, paid leave, or redeploy?); brand impact from zero Las Vegas presence during construction; competitive response from mid/upper tier hotels; need to ensure new building supports modern gambling innovations and hotel standards.

questions.prompt: What are the key trade-offs for Option 2 (renovate while open)?
questions.guidance: Candidate should cover: continued revenue stream during renovation period; renovation takes longer (likely floor-by-floor); guest disturbance may cause brand damage and reduce repeat business (candidate may debate whether Las Vegas clientele are repeat visitors or once-in-a-lifetime visitors, depending on establishment tier); cash outflows are more steady; limited scope for transformation vs. ground-up rebuild.

questions.prompt: What other issues should be considered regardless of which option is chosen?
questions.guidance: Execution risk: will the project finish on time? Are there monetary penalties for the construction team for delays? What specific renovations are needed (type of gambling tables, restaurants, bars, room quality)? What lessons can be learned from competitors who have undertaken similar projects? How should the business be relaunched on completion — marketing campaign, events, PR?

brainstorming.prompt: What specific renovations or improvements should the client consider for the Las Vegas hotel?

categories.name: Casino Floor
ideas: Update to modern gambling technology and electronic table games
Introduce new gaming concepts (sports betting, e-sports betting)

categories.name: Hotel Rooms
ideas: Upgrade room quality and furnishings to compete with tier-one rivals
Add luxury suites to attract high rollers

categories.name: Food & Beverage
ideas: Partner with celebrity chefs or well-known restaurant brands
Add a variety of dining tiers (buffet to fine dining)

categories.name: Entertainment
ideas: Add a theater or entertainment venue
Host regular headline acts to drive footfall
Introduce a rooftop pool and lounge

categories.name: Brand & Marketing
ideas: Loyalty program integration across all properties

recommendation: Recommend Option 1: knock down and rebuild

Rationale: the client is cash-rich and equity-funded so revenue loss during construction is manageable; a full rebuild allows greater scope to reposition in the market and compete with tier-one hotels; a renovation-only approach limits redesign potential and risks prolonged brand damage from guest disturbance
risks: Construction overruns on time or cost
Complete loss of Las Vegas revenue and market presence during the construction period
Staff attrition if employees are let go or uncertain about their future
Competitor hotels strengthen their position while client is absent
next_steps: Engage a construction firm and obtain detailed cost and timeline estimates
Develop a staff retention and redeployment plan across the hotel chain
Design a marketing and relaunch strategy for the reopening
Benchmark against competitors who have recently completed similar rebuilds
